text:
Jaime (Sales): Heads-up — Acme's security team returned the SIG/CAIQ and flagged the BCP/DR section. They want specifics on RTO/RPO, backups, failover, and SLA commitments. Can someone draft answers? cc @Priya @Mark

Priya (InfoSec): I can take it. Do we know if customer expects Private deployment or Hosted for the PoC? That changes the wording for contractual RTO/RPO.

Jaime (Sales): Hosted API for PoC, enterprise may move to Dedicated later. For the PoC they want to see immutable backups and cross-region failover described.

Mark (Solutions): I'll draft short copy we can paste into SIG/CAIQ fields. Keep it plain and non-legal. Key facts: multi-region control plane, serving nodes are stateless, KV caches ephemeral, persistent customer metadata backed up and encrypted.

Priya (InfoSec): Suggested numbers we can state (clear that contract trumps defaults):
- Control plane: RTO ≤ 4 hours, RPO ≤ 1 hour (hosted control plane metadata)
- Serving layer (stateless inference): goal RTO ≤ 30s with automated regional failover; RPO ~ 0 for per-request state (we don't persist requests)
- Customer persistent stores (if used): baseline backup frequency daily; contractual RTO/RPO for Private/Dedicated deployments (can be 24h/24h or tighter per agreement).

Jaime (Sales): Do we commit those verbatim in SIG/CAIQ? They asked for exact phrasing.

Mark (Solutions): Paste this into the questionnaire field "Business Continuity / Disaster Recovery":
```text
Our hosted offering uses redundant control-plane services across multiple regions to enable automated failover. Serving nodes are designed to be stateless; traffic is routed through health-checked endpoints with automated failover (typical failover <30s). Customer metadata and configuration are encrypted at rest, replicated, and backed up with incremental snapshots (default RPO ≤ 1 hour and RTO ≤ 4 hours). For Dedicated/Private deployments, RTO/RPO and backup retention are contractually agreed and can include cross-region replication and configurable retention policies.
```

Priya (InfoSec): Add testing & verification: we perform quarterly DR drills for the control plane and monthly failover rehearsals in staging; backups are validated daily. Key management via KMS/HSM; customer keys supported for dedicated/private.

Mark (Solutions): Add SLA language for customer signals: Dedicated offers 99.95% SLA on provisioned throughput (credit-based remedies). Hosted enterprise SLA can be added via an addendum for pilots or production. For PoC usage we typically operate on standard platform availability with monitoring and support; we can offer a short-term SLA if they require it.

Jaime (Sales): They also asked about default backup retention windows — what's out-of-the-box?

Priya (InfoSec): Default retention: 30 days for incremental snapshots, 90 days for monthly full snapshots. Retention adjustable via contract. All backups encrypted; customer-managed keys available for enterprise plans.

Leo (SRE): Ops note to include: failover path uses DNS + Anycast + health-proxied routing. In our internal tests median failover ~12s, 95th <60s. We'll include that as "typical observed" numbers but keep contractual commitments to the conservative figures above.

Jaime (Sales): Great — I'll paste Mark's block + Priya/Leo bullets into the SIG and send back. Thanks :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: automated note — thread tagged for sales-security review.

Priya (InfoSec): lgtm. Jaime — if they push exact numbers into the PoC contract ping me, I'll sign off.

Mark (Solutions): Sample contract clause we use for Dedicated (can include in answers if they ask for contractual wording): `SLA: 99.95% monthly uptime with credit-based remedies; RTO 4 hours for control plane; RPO 1 hour for metadata backups.` Want me to add that into the questionnaire?

Jaime (Sales): Yes please. I'll update the SIG/CAIQ now and send to Acme. End.
